info.title: Sessionboard Public API
info.description: REST API for managing sessions, speakers, contacts, sponsors, exhibitors, and event data on the Sessionboard platform.

tags.name: Sessions workspace
tags.description: The self-serve Sessionboard Sessions workspace: Home, events, the call for speakers (text, open, close), submissions and decisions, the agenda (times, rooms, tracks, sponsor tags, adding and importing sessions, publishing), speakers and sponsors. Organization-level: paths start at `/v1/organization/{orgId}/sessions-workspace`, and the same operations are served under `/v1/sessions-workspace` with the organization taken from the token. Reads need `read:sessions`, writes `write:sessions`. A key restricted to particular events cannot use it. Opening the call and publishing the agenda wait for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`). Sessions sends no decision emails and has no speaker portal.

get.description: The workspace at a glance: the organization, the plan tier (`self_serve` or `enterprise`), every Sessions event (newest first) with its counts and its call for speakers, the setup checklist for the newest event, and what only the Sessionboard platform includes, each with `locked` for your plan. Reads only. Requires `read:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/sessions-workspace`.

Every Sessions event in the organization, newest first, with its counts. Reads only. Requires `read:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/sessions-workspace/events`.

post.description: Creates an event with its one call for speakers (closed until opened, the standard questions, no speaker portal), a few rooms and tracks to rename, and an empty agenda. On a self-serve plan, refused past the plan's events in the last 12 months (`403 enterprise_only`, `upgrade: events`). The token's user must be an organization admin. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/sessions-workspace/events`.

get.description: One event: dates, timezone, location, counts and its call for speakers; its rooms, tracks and formats; its sponsors; and, on a self-serve plan, `limits` (speakers per event, read-only). Reads only. Requires `read:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}`.

put.description: Changes the name, dates, timezone or location. Only the fields you send change. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `PUT /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}`.

What speakers see above the questions: the title, the welcome text (plain text; a blank line starts a new paragraph) and when the call closes by itself (an empty string clears it). Changes show on the public form at once. Sends nothing. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `PUT /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/cfp`.

closeAt.description: ISO 8601 date and time, or an empty string to clear it.

post.summary: Ask to open the call for speakers
post.description: Asks a person to open the call. Opening makes the public form take submissions, so an API call never opens it directly: it answers `202` with `status: needs_approval` and a link, and nothing changes until a person approves it in Sessionboard Sessions. It then runs as that person. Do not call again for the same change. A trial opens without a card. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/cfp/open`.

Closes the call now. Submissions already in stay; the public link shows the call as closed. Sends nothing. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/cfp/close`.

get.description: The event's sessions with their speakers, decision, time, room, track and sponsor tags, and whether each came through the call (`submitted`). Reads only. Requires `read:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/sessions`.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: `submissions`: only what came through the call.

post.description: Adds a session the organizer invited (a keynote, a panel, a break), accepted at once, with its speakers. A speaker is matched by email across the organization. Speakers count toward the plan's speakers per event (`403 enterprise_only`, `upgrade: speakers`). Sends nothing. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/sessions`.

put.description: Changes a session's title, description, start and end (an empty string clears the time), room, track, format, or its sponsor tags (`sponsorIds` is the full list). Only the fields you send change. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `PUT /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/sessions/{sessionId}`.

roomId.description: A room id, or empty for no room.

trackId.description: A track id, or empty for no track.

formatId.description: A format id, or empty for none.

put.description: Records the organizer's decision: `accept`, `decline` or `undecided`. No email is sent to the speakers. Accepting is refused past the plan's speakers per event (`403 enterprise_only`, `upgrade: speakers`). Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `PUT /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/sessions/{sessionId}/decision`.

get.description: Everyone on an accepted session, with their email and sessions, and `limit`, the speakers the plan includes per event (`null` on the platform). Reads only. Requires `read:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/speakers`.

put.description: Replaces the room list, in order. Keep a room by sending its `id` (a new name renames it); add one with a name only. A room left out is removed, unless a session still uses it: then nothing changes (`409`, `code: in_use`). Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `PUT /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/rooms`.

Replaces the track list, in order, like the rooms. A track a session still uses cannot be removed (`409`, `code: in_use`). Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `PUT /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/tracks`.

post.description: Adds a sponsor to the event's list (a name and optionally a website). Tag it on sessions with `sponsorIds` on Update a session. Up to 50 sponsors per event. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/sponsors`.

delete.description: Takes a sponsor off the event's list and off its sessions. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `DELETE /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/sponsors/{sponsorId}`.

get.description: Every accepted session with its time (read it in the event's `timezone`), room, track and sponsor tags; the rooms, tracks, formats and sponsors; and `agenda_published_at`. Reads only. Requires `read:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/agenda`.

post.description: Asks a person to publish the agenda and speaker wall to the organizer's website. Because it is public, an API call answers `202` with `status: needs_approval`; once a person approves it in Sessionboard Sessions, the agenda is published and its embed snippets are on the agenda page. The embeds then show changes as they are made. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/agenda/publish`.

Adds sessions and their speakers from rows (up to 300): a title, and optionally a description, a track (a new name adds a track) and speakers. A title already on the event is skipped, so a second import makes no duplicates. Imported sessions are accepted unless `status` is `pending`. Speakers count toward the plan. Sends nothing. Requires `write:sessions`. Refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/sessions-workspace/events/{eventId}/import`.

ApiKey.name: x-access-token
ApiKey.description: Organization API token. Generate from Organization Settings → API Tokens.

BearerToken.description: OAuth 2.1 access token. Obtained via the OAuth PKCE flow at `/oauth/token`.

SessionsOrgId.name: orgId
SessionsOrgId.description: Your organization ID. Any other organization returns `404`.

SessionsWorkspaceSource.description: Optional on every write: which assistant is calling and what the person asked it. Recorded with the change in the organization's activity and on any approval request.

SessionsWorkspaceCall.description: An event's one call for speakers.

logo_url.description: Set on the platform; Sessions does not take logos.

submitted.description: Came through the call for speakers.

enterprise.description: What only the Sessionboard platform includes.

upgrade.description: With `enterprise_only`: what needs a bigger plan or the platform (`events`, `speakers`, `review_plans`, `forms`, …).

url.description: Where a person approves or declines it in Sessionboard Sessions (`/sessions/{orgId}/approvals?id={approval_id}`).

SessionsWorkspaceReadForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED`: the token lacks `read:sessions`.
- `ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED`: the key is restricted to particular events; use a key without an event restriction.
- `FORBIDDEN`: the token's user is not an active member of the organization.

SessionsWorkspaceWriteForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED`: the token lacks `write:sessions`.
- `ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED`: the key is restricted to particular events.
- `code: enterprise_only` with `upgrade`: the self-serve plan does not include it (another event this year, more speakers on the event); a person chooses a bigger plan or talks to us about the platform.
- `code: trial_ended` or `plan_ended`: the self-serve plan is read-only; everything can still be read.
- `FORBIDDEN` with no `code`: the token's user is not an organization admin.

speakers.summary: Past the plan's speakers per event

value.message: This event has reached the speakers your plan includes. Bigger events are part of Growth or the Sessionboard platform.
Your Sessions trial has ended. Choose a plan to keep going.

SessionsWorkspaceNotFound.description: `NOT_FOUND`: `orgId` is not the token's organization, or the event, session or sponsor is not in it.

SessionsWorkspaceBadRequest.description: `VALIDATION_ERROR`: the body or a path id does not match the schema. `source` is always accepted.

SessionsWorkspaceInUse.description: `code: in_use`: a room or track left out still has sessions. Nothing changed; move them first.

SessionsWorkspacePaused.description: A person has paused connected assistants for the organization (`code: AGENT_WRITES_PAUSED`); writes wait until they resume it in Sessionboard.

SessionsWorkspaceTooManyRequests.description: The token's request limit (100 requests per 15 minutes by default) or, for writes, its daily write quota. Wait `Retry-After` seconds.

SessionsWorkspaceNeedsApproval.description: Waiting for a person: nothing was published. `payload.url` opens the request in Sessionboard Sessions, where a person approves or declines it. An approved request runs as that person.
